results.name: single_example_multiple_targets_rate
results.description: Yes rate on one-example sets (example > 1) for non-example targets that are multiples of the example (6->18, 11->55, 25->100); observed above null means the neglect model still under-generalizes a lone example to its multiples rule (below = over-generalizes).
results.code:
# name: single_example_multiple_targets_rate
# description: Yes rate on one-example sets (example > 1) for non-example targets that are multiples of the example (6->18, 11->55, 25->100); observed above null means the neglect model still under-generalizes a lone example to its multiples rule (below = over-generalizes).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    x = E[:, 0]
    m = (n == 1) & (~isex) & (x > 1) & (np.mod(t, np.where(x > 0, x, 1)) == 0)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: in_minus_out_range_3plus
results.description: For sets with 3+ examples, non-example-target yes rate inside [min,max] of the examples minus outside it; observed above null means people confine generalization to the examples' range more than the model (below = model over-confines).
results.code:
# name: in_minus_out_range_3plus
# description: For sets with 3+ examples, non-example-target yes rate inside [min,max] of the examples minus outside it; observed above null means people confine generalization to the examples' range more than the model (below = model over-confines).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    base = (n >= 3) & (~isex)
    inn = base & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx); out = base & ((t < mn) | (t > mx))
    if not inn.any() or not out.any(): return 0.0
    return float(r[inn].mean() - r[out].mean())

results.name: high_minus_low_target_rate
results.description: Across all sets, non-example-target yes rate for targets > 50 minus targets <= 50; observed above null means people favour large numbers more than the model (a magnitude bias the model lacks); below = model over-favours large targets.

def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    a = (~isex) & (t > 50); b = (~isex) & (t <= 50)
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: zero_yes_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of non-example (set,target) cells whose responses are all "no"; observed above null means people give categorical rejections more often than the model (model too graded/probabilistic for clear non-members); below = model produces too many unanimous rejections.
results.code:
# name: zero_yes_cell_fraction
# description: Fraction of non-example (set,target) cells whose responses are all "no"; observed above null means people give categorical rejections more often than the model (model too graded/probabilistic for clear non-members); below = model produces too many unanimous rejections.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"s": df["number_set"].values, "t": t, "r": r})[~isex]
    if len(d) == 0: return 0.0
    c = d.groupby(["s", "t"])["r"].max()
    return float((c == 0).mean())

results.name: two_example_same_parity_opposite_targets
results.description: For two-example sets whose examples share parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the opposite parity; observed above null means people generalize across parity more than the model from two examples (below = people restrict to the shared parity more than the model).
results.code:
# name: two_example_same_parity_opposite_targets
# description: For two-example sets whose examples share parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the opposite parity; observed above null means people generalize across parity more than the model from two examples (below = people restrict to the shared parity more than the model).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    p0 = np.mod(E[:, 0], 2); p1 = np.mod(E[:, 1], 2) if E.shape[1] > 1 else np.full(len(t), np.nan)
    m = (n == 2) & (~isex) & (p0 == p1) & (np.mod(t, 2) != p0)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: shared_last_digit_small_sets
results.description: For sets with 1-2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets sharing a last digit with some example (14->74, 28,98->8); observed above null means people generalize by last digit from few examples more than the model (below = model over-weights last-digit rules on small sets).

# description: For sets with 1-2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets sharing a last digit with some example (14->74, 28,98->8); observed above null means people generalize by last digit from few examples more than the model (below = model over-weights last-digit rules on small sets).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    ld = (np.mod(E, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (n <= 2) & (~isex) & ld
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: near_minus_far_inside_range
results.description: For sets with 3+ examples, among non-example targets inside [min,max], yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus those farther than 3; observed above null means people use numeric proximity more than the model (below = people disfavor near-neighbours relative to the model, i.e. less magnitude-based similarity).
results.code:
# name: near_minus_far_inside_range
# description: For sets with 3+ examples, among non-example targets inside [min,max], yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus those farther than 3; observed above null means people use numeric proximity more than the model (below = people disfavor near-neighbours relative to the model, i.e. less magnitude-based similarity).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    base = (n >= 3) & (~isex) & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    a = base & (dist <= 3); b = base & (dist > 3)
    if not a.any() or not b.any(): return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: within_set_target_sd_small_sets
results.description: Mean, over sets with 1-2 examples and >=5 distinct non-example targets, of the SD of per-target yes rates within the set; observed above null means people discriminate between targets of a small set more sharply than the model (below = model's small-set generalization is too all-or-none).
results.code:
# name: within_set_target_sd_small_sets
# description: Mean, over sets with 1-2 examples and >=5 distinct non-example targets, of the SD of per-target yes rates within the set; observed above null means people discriminate between targets of a small set more sharply than the model (below = model's small-set generalization is too all-or-none).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = ex.str.len().values
    E = pd.DataFrame(ex.tolist()).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    isex = (E == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); mx = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"s": df["number_set"].values, "t": t, "r": r})[(~isex) & (n <= 2)]
    if len(d) == 0: return 0.0
    c = d.groupby(["s", "t"])["r"].mean().reset_index()
    g = c.groupby("s")["r"].agg(["std", "count"])
    g = g[g["count"] >= 5]
    return float(g["std"].mean()) if len(g) else 0.0
